basis: Scene-local planning estimates at 140 words/minute. No measured alignment. Match each exact phrase to fresh audio before production.

stages.label: Baker's yeast: a single-celled fungus
stages.anchor: Named example: Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

stages.label: An outgrowth develops on the parent
stages.anchor: Budding: a daughter cell grows from an outgrowth.

stages.label: The parent copies its DNA
stages.anchor: DNA is inherited information.

stages.label: The nucleus divides by mitosis
stages.anchor: Nucleus: the compartment containing DNA.

stages.label: One nucleus enters the growing bud
stages.anchor: Copied information supplies the daughter cell.

stages.label: The daughter cell can separate
stages.anchor: No reproductive cells or nuclei fuse.

stages.label: Asexual copying supports similar information
stages.anchor: Mutations are changes in DNA.

stages.label: Rhizopus stolonifer: bread mould
stages.anchor: This is its asexual pathway.

stages.label: The fungal body includes hyphae
stages.anchor: Hyphae: thin growing threads.

stages.label: A stalk ends in a sporangium
stages.anchor: Sporangium: a spore-containing structure.

stages.label: Mitosis forms spores without fusion
stages.anchor: Formation evidence: an asexual pathway.

stages.label: Spores disperse from the parent
stages.anchor: Dispersal: movement away from the parent.

stages.label: A spore can germinate in suitable conditions
stages.anchor: Germination means beginning to grow.

stages.label: Growing hyphae develop a new fungal body
stages.anchor: Keep the spore and its new growth distinct.

stages.label: Landing somewhere does not guarantee growth
stages.anchor: Suitable moisture, nutrients and conditions are needed.

stages.label: Baker's yeast also has a sexual pathway
stages.anchor: This is a simplified named model.

stages.label: Compatible mating-type cells can join
stages.anchor: Compatibility matters.

stages.label: The nuclei fuse
stages.anchor: Fusion brings chromosome sets together.

stages.label: Chromosomes contain DNA
stages.anchor: A chromosome is a DNA-containing structure.

stages.label: Haploid: one set. Diploid: two sets.
stages.anchor: The number describes chromosome sets.

stages.label: Nuclear fusion produces a diploid cell
stages.anchor: The resulting cell has two chromosome sets.

stages.label: Any two cells do not guarantee fusion
stages.anchor: Different fungi have different arrangements.

stages.label: Diploid yeast under suitable nutrient limitation
stages.anchor: This named cell has two chromosome sets.

stages.label: Meiosis reduces two chromosome sets to one
stages.anchor: Meiosis can reshuffle inherited information.

stages.label: Haploid nuclei are packaged into spores
stages.anchor: These nuclei have one chromosome set.

stages.label: Fusion joined sets; meiosis separates them
stages.anchor: The spores belong to this sexual cycle.

stages.label: Rhizopus mitotic spores follow another pathway
stages.anchor: Do not classify by the word spore alone.

stages.label: Selected examples, with organism limits
stages.anchor: Fungi do not all share one life cycle.
